parameters.quote: Manufacturers shall report to the regulator any thermal incident involving fire, smoke, uncontrolled overheating, injury, property damage, or emergency response within 24 hours of learning of it, with a fuller investigation report within 30 days. Manufacturers shall maintain records of all thermal incidents, including incidents not meeting immediate-reporting criteria, and provide an annual summary to the regulator.

S1_incident_reporting.rule_summary: Manufacturers shall report to the regulator any thermal incident involving fire, smoke, uncontrolled overheating, injury, property damage, or emergency response within 24 hours of learning of it, with a fuller investigation report within 30 days. Manufacturers shall maintain records of all thermal incidents, including incidents not meeting immediate-reporting criteria, and provide an annual summary to the regulator.
S1_incident_reporting.final_rule_text: Manufacturers shall report to the regulator any thermal incident involving fire, smoke, uncontrolled overheating, injury, property damage, or emergency response within 24 hours of learning of it, with a fuller investigation report within 30 days. Manufacturers shall maintain records of all thermal incidents, including incidents not meeting immediate-reporting criteria, and provide an annual summary to the regulator. Affected customers must be notified promptly when an incident presents a credible safety risk to their unit or requires action; notices must include practical steps to reduce risk and a contact for assistance.

S2_thermal_testing.rule_summary: Before purchase, customers shall receive the exact per-model 55 °C test failure rate, pass/fail status, material safety limitations, any required corrective actions, and an explanation of the applicable 5% limit. Regulators shall keep company-specific failure rates confidential and shall not publish them; exceedance alone does not require a permanent market ban.
S2_thermal_testing.final_rule_text: Each model must be tested under a sustained-heat test at 55 °C. The failure rate must not exceed 5% of tested units for any model. Manufacturers shall submit per-model test methods and complete results to the regulator for compliance review; regulators shall keep company-specific failure rates confidential and shall not publish them. Before purchase, customers shall receive the exact per-model 55 °C test failure rate, pass/fail status, material safety limitations, any required corrective actions, and an explanation of the applicable 5% limit. Regulators shall assess exceedances individually and may require corrective action, retesting, or risk-based sales restrictions; exceedance alone does not require a permanent market ban. Any restriction shall be proportionate to the risk and reviewed after corrective action or retesting. Retesting is required after a material design or manufacturing change and at least annually.

S3_remote_shutoff.rule_summary: Remote emergency shut-off shall be required on all new home battery units from 24 months after adoption of this standard. For units already installed, manufacturers shall offer a retrofit or equivalent safe solution and complete it within 6 years after adoption. S3_remote_shutoff.final_rule_text: Remote emergency shut-off shall be required on all new home battery units from 24 months after adoption of this standard. Manufacturers shall provide a secure, tested shut-off capability and clear instructions for its use. For units already installed, manufacturers shall offer a retrofit or equivalent safe solution and complete it within 6 years after adoption. Where retrofit is infeasible, the manufacturer shall notify the owner and provide an alternative risk-reduction plan for regulator review.

parameters.quote: New home battery units shall include built-in fire suppression no later than 36 months after adoption of this standard.

S4_fire_suppression.rule_summary: New home battery units shall include built-in fire suppression no later than 36 months after adoption of this standard.
S4_fire_suppression.final_rule_text: New home battery units shall include built-in fire suppression no later than 36 months after adoption of this standard. Manufacturers shall document the suppression system’s performance and maintenance requirements and provide them to customers and regulators. This requirement does not apply retroactively to units already installed.

parameters.quote: Manufacturers shall promptly notify affected owners and, where a hazard may affect nearby people, provide appropriate notice to relevant local authorities and the public. A recall is mandatory when a model exceeds 8 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units in a year; regulators may also order a recall where evidence indicates an equivalent serious safety risk.

S5_customer_disclosure.rule_summary: Manufacturers shall promptly notify affected owners and, where a hazard may affect nearby people, provide appropriate notice to relevant local authorities and the public. A recall is mandatory when a model exceeds 8 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units in a year; regulators may also order a recall where evidence indicates an equivalent serious safety risk.
S5_customer_disclosure.final_rule_text: Before purchase, customers must receive clear safety information covering relevant installation, operating, maintenance, emergency, and incident-reporting instructions, plus any model-specific safety limitations or corrective actions. Manufacturers shall promptly notify affected owners and, where a hazard may affect nearby people, provide appropriate notice to relevant local authorities and the public. A recall is mandatory when a model exceeds 8 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units in a year; regulators may also order a recall where evidence indicates an equivalent serious safety risk. Manufacturers shall promptly report the basis for a recall and provide customers with a remedy and instructions.

We support confidential per-model results to regulators, but not public release of individual-company failure rates. Customers should receive model-specific safety limitations and any required corrective actions; exact failure-rate figures need not be disclosed to them. We should preserve the 5% limit while specifying a clear, evidence-based corrective-action and review process for models that exceed it.

judge_section_notes: The final S2 gives exact per-model failure rates to prospective customers and keeps them confidential from the public, which satisfies HC-1 and NW-1, but it contains no mandatory sales stop, so a model above 5% can keep selling pending regulator action (favouring Northwind's Hearth 10). S5 sets a mandatory recall at 8 per 100,000 with no transition, which exposes Halcyon's Ember 8 at 9.9. S1 reports serious incidents within 24 hours but only annually summarises other incidents, and S3's new-unit deadline of 24 months exceeds the 12-month benchmark.
